bull.b: Vertiv's operating cash flow turned sharply positive from 2022 and produced FCF of ~$2.3B TTM. This sustained cash conversion funds capex for capacity, targeted M&A, working-capital needs, and shareholder returns while supporting deleveraging — a durable source of strategic optionality.

Expanding converged systems and liquid-cooling services shifts revenue mix toward engineered, higher-content solutions with recurring service attach. That increases customer switching costs, raises lifetime value per install, and supports sustainable margin improvement versus pure hardware sales.

bull.t: Materially improved leverage and credit profile
bull.b: Leverage has come down meaningfully and reported net leverage near 0.2x gives the company financing flexibility. Improved credit metrics (and S&P 500 inclusion noted by management) lower refinancing risk and cost, enabling continued capacity investment and opportunistic M&A.

bear.b: Although leverage has declined, the company still carries significant absolute debt for a cyclical industrial business. That elevates interest-rate and refinancing sensitivity and can constrain flexibility if data-center capex cycles soften or working capital needs spike during capacity ramps.

bear.t: Regional demand volatility — EMEA and APAC timing
bear.b: Large regional swings (EMEA contraction, APAC pacing/timing issues) make revenue lumpy and increase execution risk on multi-region programs. Recovery is expected later in 2026, but regional volatility can pressure quarterly margins and delay service attach and cash conversion.

bear.t: Tariff, supply-chain and execution risks from capacity ramps
bear.b: Tariffs, multi-sourcing and labor constraints raise input-cost and delivery risks. Simultaneous inventory builds and capacity ramping can compress near-term margins and cash flow, while longer delivery windows lengthen revenue recognition and elevate project execution risk over the medium term.
